Article Title: 'No evidence of fracture': Bengal govt to probe Mamata Banerjee's 2021 'injury'
Article Text:
Suvendu accuses Mamata of faking 2021 injury

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday accused his predecessor Mamata Banerjee of faking her injury during the 2021 state assembly elections.Adhikari added that a fresh inquiry would be launched to probe Mamata Banerjee's “false claims” of injury. He claimed that there was no evidence of fracture or dislocation in the-then CM's medical report issued by treating hospital.“Mamata Banerjee faked her leg injury during campaigning in Nandigram in 2021. We have the medical report which stated that there was no evidence of fracture or dislocation. We will initiate an investigation into the matter,” PTI quoted Adhikari as saying at a press conference in Kolkata. He also displayed the TMC supremo’s medical report issued by the Bangur Institute of Neuroscience.“Her false allegation insulted the people of Nandigram. I will come out with more details after the MCC (model code of conduct) is lifted after October 9... Today, I am saying this in support of my claims made yesterday,” he added.His remarks came ahead of the Nandigram byelection scheduled for October 6. The counting of votes will be held on October 9.The Nandigram constituency was vacated by Adhikari after he defeated Mamata Banerjee in her Bhabanipore stronghold in the West Bengal assembly elections in April.He also won from Nandigram, his traditional seat, but chose to keep Bhabanipore.On March 10, 2021, Mamata Banerjee, the-then chief minister, sustained injuries to her left leg and waist while campaigning in the Reyapara area of Birulia in Nandigram.She initially alleged that a few unidentified people had deliberately pushed her against the door of her open car, causing it to slam into her left leg amid a heavy crowd.In a video message from the hospital, she said the “massive crowd” had pressed against her car while she was greeting supporters, causing her leg to be crushed and injured.The TMC supremo was diagnosed with severe bone and ligament injuries to her left ankle and foot, along with bruising and pain in her right shoulder, forearm, neck and waist. She was subsequently taken to Kolkata and admitted to the state-run SSKM Hospital.Mamata Banerjee was discharged two days later, on March 12, with her left foot in a cast. She subsequently resumed campaigning in a wheelchair.The TMC won 213 of the 294 seats in the 2021 assembly elections, while the BJP secured 77.However, the BJP won the 2026 assembly elections, securing 207 seats and forming its first government in West Bengal, while the TMC won 80 seats and was voted out of power after 15 years.
Article Summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari accuses his predecessor Mamata Banerjee of faking her injury during the 2021 state assembly elections. He claimed that there was no evidence of fracture or dislocation in the-then CM's medical report issued by treating hospital.

Article Title: Jammu-Srinagar highway: 1 killed, 56 injured in twin accidents in J&K's Ramban
Article Text:
Passenger bus travelling from Srinagar to Jammu lost control. (Photo credit: X)

A tourist from West Bengal was killed and 56 people, including nine security personnel, were injured in two separate road accidents on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway in J&K’s Ramban district on Saturday.The accidents occurred within half an hour and involved a passenger bus carrying tourists and a security vehicle that was on its way to assist in the rescue operation, PTI reported citing officials.The first accident took place around 8.50am near Maroog when a passenger bus travelling from Srinagar to Jammu lost control and collided with a hillside, officials saidThe bus, which had a West Bengal registration, was carrying tourists returning from a holiday in Kashmir. A woman passenger, identified as Jamuna from West Bengal, died in the accident, while 47 others were injured.Four of the injured: Suchitra, Lakshwanti, Kedar Patra and Fouji Ram, were referred to Government Medical College (GMC) Hospital in Jammu for treatment. The remaining injured passengers were stable and were expected to be discharged within a few hours, officials said.After receiving information about the bus accident, a Quick Reaction Team (QRT) of the Jammu and Kashmir Police and CRPF was rushed from the District Police Lines in Ramban to assist with the rescue operation.However, the security vehicle overturned near Kela Morh while travelling to the accident site, injuring six police personnel and three CRPF personnel, officials said. All nine injured security personnel were stable, they added.Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha expressed grief over the death and assured that the seriously injured would receive the best possible medical treatment."Deeply anguished by the tragic bus accident in Ramban, in which one person lost her life. Heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family. Spoke with DC (Deputy Commissioner) Ramban to ensure best possible treatment for the seriously injured shifted to GMC Jammu. Praying for their speedy recovery," Sinha said in a post on X.

Article Title: CJP protest: Scuffle breaks out near Shiv Sena Bhavan as supporters return from stir; watch
Article Text:
A scuffle erupted near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after a protest





MUMBAI: A scuffle broke out near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) returned from a protest at Shivaji Park.A video from the spot shows protesters arguing, with some allegedly hitting each other.The situation soon turned physical, prompting police to intervene and disperse those involved. Mumbai Police later said the situation was under control and peaceful.The incident followed a CJP protest at Shivaji Park over the party’s demands concerning Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.Before the protest, a Dadar resident had opposed the demonstration. “They are doing it forcefully. This protest should not take place,” the resident said, adding that such demonstrations disturb peace in the area.The CJP has been demanding Kumar’s resignation and changes to the functioning and appointment process of the Election Commission. The Election Commission currently lists Gyanesh Kumar as the Chief Election Commissioner.Mumbai Police had earlier denied permission for the CJP to hold its October 2 protest at Shivaji Park. The party later announced a “Jail Bharo Andolan”.Meanwhile, a 75-year-old Thane resident died after suffering a heart attack while attending the CJP protest at Shivaji Park on Friday evening.The deceased was identified as Gopalakrishna Subbaiya Pillai, a resident of Dosti West County in Thane.Pillai arrived at Shivaji Park around 4.30pm to attend the protest. Around 5pm, he complained of chest pain. His friend and police personnel at the spot helped take him to Sushrusha Hospital in Shivaji Park.Police personnel tried to revive him with CPR before he was taken to the hospital, where he died while undergoing treatment. Police said doctors attributed his death to a heart attack.
Article Summary: A scuffle broke out near Shiv Sena Bhavan in Dadar after supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party returned from a protest at Shivaji Park. A video from the spot shows protesters arguing, with some allegedly hitting each other. The situation soon turned physical, prompting police to intervene and disperse those involved. Mumbai Police later said the situation was under control and peaceful.

Article Title: Flydubai attack: Co-pilot identified as Hamam Alhamami was barred from flying in Oman over 'extremist views'
Article Text:
As per reports, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. His alleged views are being examined as part of a wider investigation into possible Islamic radicalisation and terrorist motives

Removed from Oman Air training role

Pro-Palestinian material found among belongings

Questions over clearance for Tel Aviv flight

Who is Hamam Alhamami?

What happened aboard flydubai flight

The Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv has been identified as Hamam Alhamami. He was barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views.Al Arabiya English, citing sources, reported that he had spent much of his time outside Oman, particularly in Syria, where he was allegedly influenced by extremist ideas before travelling to the UAE.The revelations follow a CNN report that Alhamami had been removed from a training role at Oman Air, Oman's national carrier, last year. However, he was later given another role at the airline, the report said, citing a regional diplomatic source familiar with the matter.Further reports have raised questions about Alhamami's alleged ideological views. i24 News, citing an Emirati source, reported that leaflets and publications from “Free Palestine” groups, along with other pro-Palestinian material, were found among his belongings.According to the report, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. The report said investigators were examining the material as part of a broader probe into his alleged Islamic radicalisation and possible terrorist motives.The reports have also raised questions about how Alhamami was cleared to serve on a Tel Aviv-bound flight despite being an Omani citizen. Oman does not recognise Israel and has no diplomatic relations with the country.An Israeli official told CNN that several agencies, including Shin Bet, Mossad, the military and the Transportation Ministry, were investigating how Alhamami came to be part of the flight crew.According to the report, Alhamami is an Omani citizen. He was born in the United Arab Emirates to an Omani father and Syrian mother and spent several years of his life in the UAE. The Jerusalem Post, citing sources close to the investigation, reported that he did not hold a second nationality.CNN reported that Alhamami had worked for flydubai for only eight months. He had previously worked for Royal Air Maroc, Morocco's national carrier.Alhamami was transferred from Saudi Arabia to the UAE after the aircraft made an emergency landing in Tabuk. He is facing a terrorism investigation in the UAE.The September 30 incident took place aboard a flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Alhamami allegedly attacked Captain Machchhar inside the cockpit in what is being investigated as a possible terror-driven attempt to bring down the aircraft.The confrontation triggered a steep descent, with the aircraft dropping approximately 16,000 feet within two minutes before a hijacking distress signal was transmitted.Despite suffering severe injuries, Captain Machchhar resisted the attack and managed to open the cockpit door. Flight crew members and passengers then entered the cockpit and restrained Alhamami, allowing the crew to regain control of the aircraft.Two non-duty aviators who were travelling aboard the flight also helped assume control of the aircraft. The plane subsequently made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, with all 180 occupants disembarking safely.
Article Summary: Hamam Alhamami is the Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv. He was barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views. Pro-Palestinian material was found among his belongings, according to reports.

Article Title: Of 97 left out in Goa, 88 are back, 3 others are Portuguese citizens: EC
Article Text:
Goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories, as well as their kids and grandchildren, can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents.

NEW DELHI: The office of the Goa chief electoral officer on Thursday said 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ECINet issue have been added back after their duly filled Form 6 was accepted. However, he also revealed that three of these 97 electors are Portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside India."In respect of voters who are currently residing outside India, officials are making efforts to establish and maintain contact with them for necessary action," the CEO said while sharing the status report on the 97 cases on X.Section 9 of the Constitution disallows dual citizenship. Goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories, as well as their kids and grandchildren, can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents. Portugal recognises dual citizenship; however, since dual citizenship is not allowed in India, anybody who acquires a foreign passport must surrender his Indian passport.As per Sec 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, a person's Indian citizenship automatically ceases upon acquiring foreign citizenship.Thus, three of the Portuguese passport holders in Goa may be classified as non-citizens, making them ineligible to be enrolled as Indian electors, said a source.Incidentally, Portuguese passport holders form 3% of the cohort of 97 electors for which the Goa CEO had repeatedly written to the EC after the ERO could not add them back via ERONet, leading the ECs to also raise questions on why access for such changes was 'centralised' and not available to the field officers. The issue was further amplified by the opposition parties after The Indian Express reported on the alleged internal notes of the election commissioners in this regard.EC sources on Thursday said the due diligence by the ERO the second time around may have served the purpose of SIR, as it is aimed at eliminating ineligible persons from the voters' list. Also, the fact that the issue was detected at the ERO level proves that the absolute right to add or delete a voter, based on verification, remains with the field officers, an EC officer told TOI.
Article Summary: 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ECINet issue have been added back after their duly filled Form 6 was accepted. Three of these 97 electors are Portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside India. Since dual citizenship is not allowed in India, anybody who acquires a foreign passport must surrender his Indian passport.

Article Title: Unsolicited advice to Supreme Court lands trial judge in trouble
Article Text:
After reading the letter, which was placed before a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran, the court expressed shock over its contents, which were uncalled for and directed its registry to ask the judge why he wrote what he wrote.

NEW DELHI: It sounds inconceivable that a trial judge will advise the top court of the country on how to decide a case. But it happened recently, and the judge is now in trouble, with the Supreme Court seeking an explanation from him for advising it on when to grant bail.The case pertains to the bail petition of an accused from West Bengal who has been an undertrial prisoner for the last five years, and the apex court, while rejecting his plea, had asked the trial court to complete the proceedings within three months. The order, which was passed on May 11, directed the trial court to file a report after disposal of the case.As the trial court could not honour the SC order, the judge wrote to the apex court seeking more time to conclude the trial. But the judge, the additional district and sessions judge, 3rd court, North 24 Parganas at Barasat, also gave some unsolicited advice to the apex court on bail jurisprudence - when to grant bail and when not.After reading the letter, which was placed before a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran, the court expressed shock over its contents, which were uncalled for and directed its registry to ask the judge why he wrote what he wrote.The bench, however, did not reveal the exact wording of the letter but noted in its order that the judge conveyed words of advice."We are quite disturbed with the manner in which the trial judge has addressed a letter to this court requesting some more time. It is not for the presiding officer to convey words of advice as to when this court should grant bail and should not grant bail. The last two paragraphs of the letter are something which we have not appreciated. Registry to call for an appropriate explanation from the presiding officer at the earliest," SC said.The judge had written the letter dated Aug 11 addressed to the assistant registrar, Supreme Court, and prayed for some more time to complete the trial. Fixing the time for completion of the trial, SC in May had noted the case was proceeding at a snail's pace and asked that the trial be expedited as the accused had been languishing in jail for the last five years.Referring to a Calcutta HC order which had rejected the bail plea in March, saying all witnesses would be examined by the end of April, SC had said in its May order, "Although the HC was quite confident the remaining 12 witnesses would be examined by May 1, yet it seems not a single witness has been examined... We give one last chance to the state to proceed further with the recording of evidence of the remaining witnesses. We direct the trial court to see to it that the trial is completed within three months from today without fail."
Article Summary: The case pertains to the bail petition of an accused from West Bengal who has been an undertrial prisoner for the last five years. The apex court had asked the trial court to complete the proceedings within three months. The trial court could not honour the SC order, the judge wrote to the apex court seeking more time.

Article Title: Pacific to pacify ties? Washington sends US admiral to India as relations face strain
Article Text:
Samuel Paparo's visit comes after a run of statements in Washington.

Press release by the US Embassy in India.

What Washington has put on record

The China question in the background

NEW DELHI: American admiral Samuel J. Paparo, who leads US Indo-Pacific Command, is in India from 3 to 8 October. It is his second visit this year.The US Embassy said the trip is meant to push forward the "major defense partnership" and deepen cooperation between the two militaries.Its list of topics includes digital transformation, emerging technologies and regional strategic stability. It also names "defense energy resilience" and an "increasingly competitive technology landscape", though it does not spell out what either would involve.On his earlier trip, Paparo visited Delhi, Chandimandir and Bengaluru. He met the Chief of Defence Staff and the Navy chief, and discussed security along India's western and northern borders.Last month, Paparo conducted a series of key bilateral and multilateral meetings on the sidelines of the 28th Indo-Pacific Chiefs of defence conference in Victoria, Canada, held from August 31 to September 2.According to the US Pacific Command (US PACOM), Paparo highlighted "the importance of strong bilateral and multilateral relationships in advancing regional security and deterrence".Throughout the conference, the US commander engaged in discussions with the Defence Cooperation Council and the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad), and joined military leadership from Asean nations.Paparo also connected with defence counterparts from Australia and the United Kingdom for an Aukus dialogue, and conferred with Adm. Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, chair of the Nato Military Committee.US Pacific Command noted that Paparo carried out bilateral discussions focused on "strengthening operational cooperation, information-sharing, maritime security and readiness across the Indo-Pacific" with senior representatives from numerous partner nations.The participating countries included Bangladesh, Brunei, Cambodia, Canada, France, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, Mongolia, New Zealand, the Republic of Korea, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam.Paparo's visit comes after a run of statements in Washington. An update on how the 2026 National Defense Strategy is being carried out, sent to the Senate Armed Services Committee, places India under the heading of burden-sharing, the idea that allies and partners should take on more of the load."Finally, and crucially given its regional standing and power, we are also building on our strong defence relationship with India, with the recent signature of a 10-year bilateral defence framework and a separate framework to strengthen undersea cooperation," the update said.Testifying before lawmakers in April, Paparo said the relationship with India had seen "transformative growth through increasingly complex military exercises, defence sales, and strategic dialogue".However, the recent Trump tariffs and the punitive measures against India for buying Russian oil, and a stuck trade deal has undoubetly strained the ties between both nations.Paparo had also pointed to cooperation on maritime security and underwater awareness, including India's planned purchase of MQ-9B drones through US foreign military sales. He also described India as one of the partners he visits and coordinates with most often.He said India "continues to be a source of stability within South Asia", and cited its investments in Sri Lanka and its agreements with Mauritius, which he said help keep strategic infrastructure "free of adversarial influences". On Pakistan, he noted that recent military exchanges had extended beyond traditionally disputed areas, but said India's main focus remained "maintaining deterrence and credible warfighting capability within the region writ large. "None of this is discussed in isolation from China as Paparo himself has said Beijing's actions, along with its deepening ties to Russia and North Korea, make for a complex challenge to regional stability. He calls alliances and partnerships Washington's "greatest asymmetric advantage", and the Quad, which brings together the US, India, Japan and Australia, is part of that picture. Though Quad his been pushed to a back burner under the Tump 2.0.At a regional security conference in Malaysia, Paparo said some actors were using "false claims of legitimacy" to justify coercion. "That's not the rule of law. That's the rule by law. That distinction between law as a tool of order versus law as a weapon of raw power, is the defining fault line of our time," he said. He added that the US was deterring China "through strength, not through confrontation".In the South China Sea, Manila has accused Beijing of dangerous manoeuvres, water cannon attacks and attempts to block resupply missions around a disputed shoal. China denies this. Philippine defence secretary Gilberto Teodoro said, "China is everywhere … this is a matter of concern," and pointed to a recent Chinese ballistic missile launch into the Pacific.At the congressional hearing, Representative Adam Smith said partners needed reassurance. "We need to maintain those relationships. We need to let those folks know that we are there and they can depend on us," he said.
Article Summary: American admiral Samuel J. Paparo, who leads US Indo-Pacific Command, is in India from 3 to 8 October. It is his second visit this year. US Embassy said the trip is meant to push forward the "major defense partnership" and deepen cooperation.

Article Text:
Acquitting a person convicted by a trial court and Chhattisgarh HC for illegally transporting 32 bulls under Chhattisgarh Agricultural Cattle Preservation Act, 2004, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said police have failed to establish the intention of the accused.

NEW DELHI: At a time when vigilante groups are active in stopping cattle smuggling purportedly to prevent slaughter, the Supreme Court has ruled that the police cannot presumptively invoke stringent provisions of anti-cattle slaughter laws against people for mere illegal transportation of bovine animals.Acquitting a person convicted by a trial court and Chhattisgarh HC for illegally transporting 32 bulls under Chhattisgarh Agricultural Cattle Preservation Act, 2004, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said police have failed to establish the intention of the accused that cattle were being transported for slaughter. The prosecution said the intercepted truck did not have any document that authorised the driver and cleaner to transport cattle from Chhattisgarh to Odisha."The mere fact that the transport was not accompanied by any documents cannot lead to a presumption that it was for slaughter," SC said. "We find no reason to uphold the conviction, especially when a veterinary doctor and the 'Gaushala Committee' chief said before the court that the seized cattle were fit for use in agriculture."
Article Summary: Supreme Court rules that police cannot invoke stringent provisions of anti- cattle slaughter laws against people for mere illegal transportation of bovine animals. Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said police have failed to establish the intention of the accused.

Article Title: Cases clubbed only after CJI spoke to presiding judges
Article Text:
The contempt petition was initiated for the alleged violation of the SC's May 23, 2025, judgement directing the gradual reduction and eventual phasing out of IPS officers' deputation to CAPFs and is pending before a bench headed by Justice Ujjal Bhuyan.

NEW DELHI: The sound and fury in the Supreme Court Wednesday over the clubbing of two petitions - one seeking the initiation of contempt proceedings for the violation of an earlier SC judgement and the other challenging the validity of a new law - both on the deputation of IPS officers in the central armed police forces (CAPFs), has turned out to be much ado about nothing.The contempt petition was initiated for the alleged violation of the SC's May 23, 2025, judgement directing the gradual reduction and eventual phasing out of IPS officers' deputation to CAPFs and is pending before a bench headed by Justice Ujjal Bhuyan.Another petition, which challenged the validity of the new CAPF Act, which was enacted subsequent to the SC judgement and permitted the deputation of IPS officers to CAPFs, is before another bench headed by Justice Manoj Misra.On September 30, the contempt petition listed before Justice Bhuyan was abruptly dropped from the notified list of cases, and, subsequently, both the contempt petition and the writ petition were listed before a special bench of Justices Misra and Bhuyan. This led to an uproar before the special bench. Senior advocate Shyam Divan said, "You cannot have a listed matter plucked off the board. This is an all-India court.People make travel arrangements and come here from all over the country. Why should a matter which is listed be removed during the course of the day? Once the cause list is mentioned and notified in the Supreme Court of India, no one can fiddle with it." Senior advocate Guru Krishna Kumar echoed Divan's grievance.However, it transpired that additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati had requested that the two petitions be clubbed and be placed for hearing before any one of the two benches on the ground that the new law was the defence of the Union govt in contempt and suggested that it would be better if the two cases were heard together.SC registry sources said following this, the CJI consulted the presiding judges - Justices Misra and Bhuyan - before constituting the special bench and placing both the matters before it.However, Justice Misra faulted the ASG for not informing the opposite side prior to making the request to the CJI, which led to such a situation. The CJI could not be contacted, as he is abroad.The SC registry, from which an explanation was sought, filed a report on clubbing of the two cases. The bench of Justices Misra and Bhuyan said in its order, "The explanation tendered by the registry is accepted and taken on record. The same shall be kept in a sealed cover by the concerned section." It posted both the contempt petition and the writ petition for hearing together on Oct 15.
Article Summary: The contempt petition was initiated for the alleged violation of the SC's May 23, 2025, judgement directing the gradual reduction and eventual phasing out of IPS officers' deputation to CAPFs. Another petition, which challenged the validity of the new CAPF Act, which was enacted subsequent to the SC judgement, is before another bench headed by Justice Manoj Misra.

NEW DELHI: Protests demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar intensified across Delhi and Mumbai on Friday, with around 700 people detained in the national capital and thousands gathering at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park despite police denying permission for the demonstrations.The protests, involving opposition parties, student organisations and youth groups, centred on alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and claims of mass voter deletions.In Delhi, AAP leaders Atishi, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Sanjeev Jha, AISA president Neha Bora, CPI(M) leaders M A Baby and Brinda Karat, CPI national secretary P Sandosh Kumar, RJD leader Manoj Jha, social activist Yogendra Yadav, DYFI president A A Rahim and former JNUSU president Aishe Ghosh were among those detained.Shortly after being detained, AISA national president Neha Bora urged protesters to return to Jantar Mantar and continue the demonstration.“All comrades, please return to Jantar Mantar and stand together for democracy and our right to vote. Do not be intimidated. Do not be silenced. Our peaceful protest continues,” Bora said.AAP’s Atishi, Sanjay Singh, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Sanjeev Jha were also detained as protesters attempted to reach Jantar Mantar.Bharadwaj was seen lying on the road while protesting against the police action.Atishi said the protesters were demonstrating peacefully to protect democracy and the right to vote.“When the British ruled India, Gandhiji fought for people's right to vote. Today, when we have that right, Gyanesh Kumar is trying to take it away,” she said.She later said protesters were taken away in buses and detained at the Fatehpur Beri police station.“We are not afraid of Modiji's police. We will continue to fight to protect the right to vote. The fight against vote theft will continue. The EC's system will have to be corrected and Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign,” Atishi said.Bharadwaj later said more than 500 people had reached Jantar Mantar before the scheduled protest and posted, “GenZ rocks.”Police said around 700 people were detained from Jantar Mantar and nearby areas. A police source told PTI that around 700 SFI members trying to reach Jantar Mantar at around 11 am were stopped at the Ashoka Road roundabout, with many detained.Protesters from the AAP, AISA, SFI, NSUI, IYC and other student and youth organisations attempted to move towards Jantar Mantar but were stopped at several locations, including Firoz Shah Road and Ashoka Road.Police repeatedly made public announcements asking people not to assemble at Jantar Mantar, saying no gathering had been permitted there.The protesters raised slogans including “Ek kachori, do samosa, Gyanesh tumhara kya bharosa” and “Gali gali mein shor hai, Modi-Gyanesh vote chor hai”, while placards carried messages such as “Resign Do”.The Indian Youth Congress marched from its office on Raisina Road towards Jantar Mantar, with protesters wearing masks bearing the faces of Kumar and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.IYC president Uday Bhanu Chib said the Election Commission was responsible for protecting the sanctity of every vote.“We are protesting because the EC is responsible for protecting the sanctity of every vote. When questions are being raised within the commission itself over decisions concerning the electoral roll, the country deserves answers and accountability,” Chib said.The Delhi Metro said entry and exit gates at 12 stations were closed during the day as part of security arrangements. These included Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat and Janpath. Internet services were also suspended in central Delhi.AAP’s Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh was stopped at North Avenue while heading towards the protest and later said he was sitting on a dharna in front of the Mahatma Gandhi statue on the Parliament premises against “vote theft”.Bharadwaj questioned the need for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar, saying the AAP had submitted letters seeking permission around six days earlier and claimed that police had not taken a decision.In Mumbai, thousands attended a protest organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Shivaji Park, despite police denying permission for the gathering.CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke warned of “Jantar Mantar 2.0” if Kumar did not resign and called for a nationwide mobilisation.“If Gyanesh Kumar does not resign, the Gen Z of the entire nation will go to Delhi. There will be Jantar Mantar 2.0,” Dipke said, giving a call for “Chalo Delhi”.CJP leader Ajinkya Shinde demanded Kumar’s resignation and criminal proceedings. The party also called for the freezing of the 2025 voter lists and the abolition of the 2023 law laying down the procedure for appointing Election Commissioners.Dipke also said, “Appointment of CEC should be transparent; there should be involvement of civil society.”Protesters carrying tricolours and placards with messages including “Gyanesh BRO, JUST RESIGN” and “Gaddaar Gyaanu Must Go” gathered in the area.Veteran actors Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi, filmmakers Vishal Bhardwaj and Hansal Mehta, singer-music director Vishal Dadlani and Tushar Gandhi, Mahatma Gandhi’s great-grandson, were present at the Mumbai protest.The Shiv Sena (UBT) extended support to the agitation, while the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) also supported the CJP’s protest.Police in both Delhi and Mumbai had denied permission for the proposed protests.In Delhi, prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita were in force across the New Delhi district, restricting public meetings or assemblies of five or more people, processions, demonstrations, picketing and dharnas without prior written permission.The Delhi Police said the restrictions were imposed to ensure public safety, maintain public order and facilitate smooth traffic movement.In Mumbai, police said they were not authorised to permit the Shivaji Park gathering in view of a 2013 Bombay High Court order and described the area as a silence zone.Despite the restrictions, protesters reached Shivaji Park, while police and security forces were deployed in large numbers and routes from Dadar railway station were barricaded.The agitation intensified after media reports claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months concerning decisions and procedures related to the SIR exercise and other electoral matters.The reported objections included issues concerning voter deletions, Form 6 and access to electoral-roll databases.The Election Commission rejected the suggestion that the objections amounted to institutional dissent, saying operational queries, inputs and suggestions raised during the draft stage were part of its standard administrative and decision-making process. The ECI said the three-member commission had taken all decisions, including those relating to the SIR, unanimously.The protests were part of a wider mobilisation by political parties, student organisations and youth groups. Demonstrations were also reported in Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Patna.AAP national media in-charge Anurag Dhanda said the party would continue its campaign.“We will not stop here. We will continue the protest across the country,” he said.CJP leader Saurav Das also criticised the detention of protesters in Delhi, saying, “Delhi Police has again resorted to brutality. We warn Delhi Police to improve or we will improve you.”
Article Summary: Protesters demand resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Around 700 people detained in Delhi, thousands gather at Mumbai's Shivaji Park. Demonstrations centred on alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Article Title: When the crew became the crisis: Air India’s 2009 mid-air brawl
Article Text:
A brawl 17 years ago brought into question flight safety

mid-air confrontation

that raised questions about

cockpit discipline

and flight safety

A fight at 30,000 feet

From argument to violence

Investigations and fallout

The recent flydubai incident has highlighted an unusual aviation danger: what happens when those responsible for flying an aircraft become part of the crisis themselves.Captain Smit Machchhar was reportedly attacked by his co-pilot during a flight, triggering a dangerous descent before the injured captain managed to open the cockpit door and allow others to intervene. The aircraft eventually landed safely.Seventeen years earlier, an Indian Airlines (then a subsidiary of Air India) flight witnessed a mid-air confrontation that raised similar questions about cockpit discipline and flight safety.On October 3, 2009, Indian Airlines flight IC-884 was carrying 106 passengers from Sharjah to Delhi via Lucknow. While cruising at around 30,000 feet over Pakistan, Captain Ranbir Arora and co-pilot Aditya Chopra became embroiled in a dispute with flight purser Amit Khanna and flight attendant Komal Singh.Reports said the confrontation spilled between the cockpit and galley while the Airbus A320 was airborne.The dispute had begun before take-off from Sharjah.In Sharjah, the cabin crew met Captain Ranbir Arora and co-pilot Aditya Chopra for a pre-flight briefing, during which the two sides were believed to have had an altercation.“The cabin crew lobby said that after the initial tension on the ground in Sharjah, when the woman crew member [Komal Singh] went into the cockpit, one of the pilots held her hand and then pushed her out of the cockpit,” according to a TOI report.She reportedly hit the cockpit door and began bleeding.Khanna then intervened, according to a cabin crew representative, who alleged that the pilots became abusive and fought with him.The pilots denied the allegation. They instead accused Khanna of misconduct that they claimed had compromised flight safety. The pilots also alleged that the molestation complaint was “aimed to protect the complainant’s purser friend — who has a commercial pilot licence (CPL) — from facing action”, the report added.After landing in Delhi, Singh filed a molestation complaint against the two pilots.There were also reports that the cockpit was briefly left effectively “unmanned” while the confrontation continued outside. Some accounts said Arora threatened to divert the aircraft to Karachi. These claims were not independently established.Singh’s allegations triggered a separate investigation. Air India set up a five-member committee, while the National Commission for Women formed a five-member panel.Delhi Police recorded Singh’s statement and registered a molestation case.Air India confirmed the fight and ordered an inquiry, while the Directorate General of Civil Aviation initiated a probe. All four crew members were grounded.The airline’s preliminary inquiry concluded that Arora and Khanna had played a greater role. Both were suspended, while Chopra and Singh remained grounded. The Indian Commercial Pilots Association questioned the action against Arora, saying the findings were not final.Air India later filed departmental chargesheets against all four. Singh was charged with participating in the altercation, failing to leave the cockpit when directed and speaking to the media in breach of company policy.Arora faced allegations including abusive language and pushing Khanna and Singh from the cockpit, while Khanna was accused of initiating the fight.An airline official said the preliminary inquiry found all four guilty of some charges, including conduct that tarnished the company's reputation.The episode became more than a workplace dispute. It showed how a personal conflict among crew members can spill into an aircraft's operational environment — and put flight safety under strain.
Article Summary: Indian Airlines flight IC-884 was carrying 106 passengers from Sharjah to Delhi via Lucknow. Captain Ranbir Arora and co-pilot Aditya Chopra became embroiled in a dispute with flight purser Amit Khanna and flight attendant Komal Singh. Reports said the confrontation spilled between the cockpit and galley.

It is only going to escalate further," he said.Dhillon also alleged that the law and order situation in Punjab was "dire" and raised the issue of crimes against Dalits."The situation in Punjab is dire. In the Chief Minister's own district, crimes against Dalits are occurring daily.Today, there is virtually no law and order left in the entire state of Punjab," he said.His remarks came as the Congress prepares to reorganise its Punjab unit ahead of the assembly polls due early next year. Warring's resignation followed longstanding differences within the state Congress.Earlier on Friday, Warring claimed that AICC Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot may have decided that it was time for him to be removed as state Congress chief.Speaking to ANI, Warring said he had already conveyed his views to Rahul Gandhi and acknowledged that he did not have concrete proof that Pilot had taken the decision."When he was appointed in charge, I went to formally congratulate him. I spoke with him for about 15 minutes that day. But I haven't met him since. Given my long journey in politics, I feel that Sachin Pilot must have decided it was time to remove 'Raja' from the post. I don't have concrete proof of this, but perhaps the General Secretary felt that Raja should be removed. Otherwise, there is no specific issue. I have conveyed what I had to say to Rahul Gandhi. There is no one left after Rahul Gandhi to whom I could explain what should or shouldn't happen," Warring said.Warring also said Gandhi showed him “a lot of love” during their meeting. According to PTI, he told Gandhi about the challenges facing the Congress in Punjab, its strengths and the political situation in the state."I met Rahul Gandhi and formally gave him my resignation," Warring told reporters after the meeting, according to PTI. He said Gandhi sought information about the political situation in Punjab, including what was happening with the government and what the Congress should be doing."He made me the state Congress chief, and I thanked him for giving me the opportunity to lead the state Congress in difficult circumstances. I assured him that I am ready to serve the party whenever the party requires me," Warring said.Warring had headed the Punjab Congress since 2022, when he succeeded Navjot Singh Sidhu. The party recently replaced Bhupesh Baghel as its AICC in-charge for Punjab and appointed Sachin Pilot in his place.Former state minister Vijay Inder Singla is among those being considered for the post of Punjab Congress chief and has emerged as a leading contender.
Article Summary: Warring resigned as Punjab Congress president on Friday after heading the state unit for more than four years. He later met Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and formally handed in his resignation. Warring claimed that AICC Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot may have decided that it was time for him to be removed.

Article Title: 'Stark gap between claims and Punjab's reality': Congress, SAD target AAP over viral video of woman allegedly on drugs
Article Text:
Viral video from Bathinda sparks fresh political row over Punjab's drug crisis. (Photo: X)

Punjab Cong targets Mann

Sukhbir Badal attacks AAP

Shah sets 2029 deadline for drug-free Punjab

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab came under fire on Friday after a viral video appeared to show a young woman in an intoxicated state at Bathinda’s grain market, triggering a fresh political row over the state’s drug menace.The Punjab Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) targeted the government over its handling of the issue. The video, which surfaced on social media, shows the woman behaving erratically in a public place.Bathinda Police said the woman has been admitted to a de-addiction centre. According to the police, she is from Faridkot and her family has been informed. Her mother has also arrived at the centre, while police said further action is being taken, as per TOI sources.Reacting to the video, Punjab Congress said on X, “The haunting visuals from Bathinda’s grain market expose the stark gap between Bhagwant Mann’s claims and Punjab’s reality. While he holds an event in Ludhiana and declares Punjab “drug-free”, these images tell a very different story. The much-hyped “Yudh Nashian Virudh” has clearly failed. Punjab is being run from Delhi, with Bhagwant Mann reduced to a puppet of Delhi’s leadership.When the government is controlled from Delhi, Punjab’s problems will never be its priority.”Punjab Congress in-charge Sachin Pilot also criticised the state government, saying, “Deeply disturbing videos emerging from Bathinda showing a youth struggling with severe drug addiction, alongside events in Sangrur district where a bereaved family seeking justice due to young man’s suicide was forcefully evicted from outside the Civil Hospital - in the home district of CM @BhagwantMann These should not be dismissed as isolated cases. They point to the AAP government’s absolute failure to address pressing issues on the ground and to fix the accountability where it matters. The AAP government has FAILED Punjab.”SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal also shared the video and targeted the Mann government.“Our daughters are Punjab’s future, strength and pride. If they are not safe from the drug menace, how will we secure Punjab’s future? The visuals coming from Bathinda grain market have shaken the conscience of Punjab. A young girl in such a pathetic condition, completely doped and behaving in a strange manner in a public place, is a horrifying reminder of how deeply the drug menace has penetrated our society. Guru-Dokhi @BhagwantMann ’s government has failed to protect our youth. Despite all the slogans and publicity around Yudh Nasheyan Virudh, drugs continue to destroy lives and now even our daughters are being swallowed by this menace. Punjab needs freedom from drugs, not a government high on its own publicity.”Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal also criticised the AAP government, saying, “When an ‘outsider’ who doesn’t know the history or geography of Punjab comes and tries to claim ~ ‘I will wipe out drugs from Punjab in 3 months’ ~ this is what happens."Earlier, SAD has also announced a fresh statewide campaign ahead of the 2027 Assembly election.The row comes amid an intensifying political battle over Punjab’s drug problem. At a rally in Jalandhar on Wednesday, Union home minister Amit Shah accused the AAP government of allowing the trade in “chitta” to flourish and said the BJP would make Punjab drug-free by December 31, 2029, if voted to power in the 2027 Assembly election.“Such a time has arisen that we have to give a call for making Punjab drug-free, because Aam Aadmi Party govt has allowed open trade of ‘chitta’ in the state. I have come to tell people of Punjab, that there are several serious issues in the state, including that of farmers, industry, law and order, women protection, but in the coming election, BJP will contest only and only on the issue of making Punjab ‘nasha mukt’ (drugs-free),” he said.“From here, I make a promise to the mothers and youths of Punjab, support BJP and vote for lotus in the upcoming assembly election and by Dec 31, 2029, Punjab will be free of drug trade,” he announced.Shah also said the BJP’s anti-drug campaign had covered all 117 Assembly constituencies through the ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatra’.The AAP, in response, questioned the Centre’s focus on Punjab and pointed to the seizure of 526 kg of heroin and methamphetamine worth more than Rs 3,000 crore in an operation involving the Gujarat Anti-Terrorist Squad and Indian Coast Guard.“Amit Shah came to Punjab today to give lectures on drugs. At the same time, 526 kg of heroin and methamphetamine worth over Rs 3,000 crore has been seized in an operation in which Gujarat ATS provided the intelligence. We have been saying that Gujarat has emerged as a major gateway for drugs in the country. This seizure once again shows the scale of the problem. If Amit Shah is serious about Nasha Mukt Bharat, he should start his Nasha Mukt Yatra from Gujarat, not Punjab,” the AAP said in a statement.The party also claimed that the Punjab government had disrupted drug supply networks and alleged that a large share of pharmaceutical drugs seized in the state originated outside Punjab.The Bathinda video is not the first purported footage to trigger discussion over drug abuse in Punjab. Several videos have circulated on social media in recent months, with users claiming they showed people under the influence of drugs, sometimes referring to a “zombie drug”.The term “zombie drug” is commonly used for xylazine, a veterinary sedative that has been found mixed with illicit drugs and is also known as “tranq” or “tranq dope”. However, the presence of xylazine or any specific drug in the Bathinda video has not been independently established.
Article Summary: Video appears to show young woman in an intoxicated state at Bathinda's grain market. Punjab Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal target the government over its handling of the issue. Police said the woman has been admitted to a de-addiction centre.

Article Title: India is 'trusted voice' for global peace: Amit Shah hails Putin's praise for PM Modi's peace efforts
Article Text:
Amit Shah hails PM Modi's peace push after Putin's 'good ideas' remark​

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Friday welcomed Russian President Vladimir Putin 's remarks praising Prime Minister Narendra Modi's efforts to resolve the Russia-Ukraine conflict, saying India has emerged as the "most trusted voice for global peace" under his leadership.In a post on X, Shah said Putin's appreciation of PM Modi 's peace efforts, coinciding with Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary, was a moment of pride for every Indian."It is a moment of pride for every Indian that Russian President Mr. Vladimir Putin has commended Prime Minister Mr. @narendramodi ji's efforts for global peace. This statement, coming on the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi ji, who gave the message of peace and non-violence to the entire world, shows that under Modi ji's leadership, India has today become the most trusted voice for global peace."Shah said PM Modi has consistently advocated dialogue and diplomacy over military confrontation amid global conflicts and instability. He also cited India's humanitarian assistance during international crises, linking it to the country's philosophy of 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam'."In this era of war, tension, and instability, Modi ji has given a message to the entire world that solutions do not emerge on the battlefield, but through dialogue and diplomacy.Be it global conflicts or any disaster, under Modi ji's leadership, India has always stepped forward first to offer help, and that is why our tradition of 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' has today gained a new identity on the global stage."That is precisely why India's stance matters in any crisis in the world today, and the whole world listens attentively to what Modi ji has to say."Putin, speaking at the Valdai Club forum on Thursday, had praised PM Modi's efforts to find a peaceful resolution to the Russia-Ukraine war, saying the Indian Prime Minister had "good ideas" for finding mutually acceptable solutions."Prime Minister Narendra Modi is one of those world leaders who, despite our very good and even friendly relations, personal good relations, constantly raises the question and asks the question about putting an end to the conflict in Ukraine," Putin said.He described PM Modi as a leader with an active interest in ending the conflict and said Russia was thankful for his efforts."We are thankful for his desire to put an end to this conflict through peaceful means and as soon as possible," Putin added.PM Modi has repeatedly called for dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the conflict, maintaining that India has adopted a principled and humanitarian approach while maintaining relations with both Moscow and Kyiv.During an interview with Japanese news outlet The Yomiuri Shimbun in August, PM Modi said both Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had shared their perspectives on the conflict with him.He reiterated India's willingness to support efforts aimed at achieving an early and lasting peace.The latest remarks come amid heightened tensions between Russia and Western countries, with Putin reiterating that Moscow had no plans to attack European nations while warning that Russia would respond to any aggression with "all weapons" at its disposal.He also accused European countries of escalating tensions through military exercises in the Baltic Sea, discussions about a possible conflict with Russia and the seizure of Russian vessels.European leaders and intelligence agencies, meanwhile, have warned that Russia could develop the capability to attack another country within the next few years, particularly if it emerges victorious from the war in Ukraine.
Article Summary: Amit Shah hails PM Modi's peace push after Putin's 'good ideas' remark. Shah: India has emerged as the "most trusted voice for global peace" under Modi's leadership. Putin described PM Modi as a leader with an active interest in ending the conflict.

Article Title: 'Consider for Ashoka Chakra': Milind Deora writes to PM Modi seeking honour for pilot Smit Machchhar
Article Text:
Pilot Smit Machchhar hailed for bravery as Deora seeks Ashoka Chakra

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha MP Milind Deora wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday urging the government to consider flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for the Ashoka Chakra for his role in averting an alleged attempt to take control of a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight."I am writing to you regarding Captam Smit Machchhar, the Mumbai-born pilot whose extraordinary courage and presence of mind during the receist Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv helped save the lives of all 174 passengers on board," Deora said in the letter."His courage has already been recognised not merely in India, but across the world. I believe that formally recognising such an act would carry significance far beyond the honour bestowed upon one Individual. It would send a powerful message, particularly to our young people, thut courage is not confined to the battlefield or to any particular profession," he added.Machchhar, a Mumbai-born pilot, was seriously injured after his co-pilot allegedly attacked him and attempted to take control of the aircraft during flydubai flight FZ1073. Despite his injuries, Machchhar continued to act to protect the 174 passengers on board, Deora said in his letter to PM Modi.The flight, carrying 174 passengers, including 27 children, transmitted emergency signals and rapidly lost altitude before diverting to Prince Sultan Bin Abdulaziz Airport in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.According to accounts of the incident, Machchhar was attacked in the cockpit, after which an Israeli passenger and a crew member managed to enter the cockpit and helped overpower the co-pilot. The UAE has launched an investigation into the incident, with the motive behind the alleged attack still under probe.Deora said Machchhar's actions went beyond the responsibilities of his profession and demonstrated "courage, selflessness and duty" in an extreme situation."The Ashoka Chakra is India's highest peacetime gallantry decoration" and is intended to recognise conspicuous bravery, valour or self-sacrifice other than in the face of the enemy, Deora said, urging the government to consider Machchhar for the honour.The appeal comes after PM Modi spoke to Machchhar over a video call and praised his courage, presence of mind and composure during the ordeal. PM Modi told him that the country was proud of his efforts to protect the lives of those onboard.During the conversation, Machchhar told PM Modi that he recites the Hanuman Chalisa whenever he faces difficulty and had done so during the tense moments aboard the flight. He also described Modi as his "biggest idol".Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had also praised Machchhar's actions, saying he helped thwart what could have been a "9/11-like" disaster.In his letter, Deora said formally recognising Machchhar would underline that courage and self-sacrifice are not confined to the battlefield or any particular profession.
Article Summary: Rajya Sabha MP Milind Deora wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday. He urged the government to consider flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for the Ashoka Chakra for his role in averting an alleged attempt to take control of a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight.Machchhar was seriously injured after his co-pilot allegedly attacked him and attempted to take Control of the aircraft.

Article Title: BSF neutralises 2 Pakistani intruders attempting to cross border in Punjab's Tarn Taran
Article Text:
(With ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Border Security Force BSF ) on Friday neutralised two Pakistani intruders attempting to enter Indian territory across the International Border (IB) in Punjab , officials said.The intruders were trying to cross into Punjab’s Tarn Taran area around noon. Their identities have yet to be ascertained.According to officials, BSF troops noticed suspicious movement in the area and challenged the intruders, repeatedly warning them to stop.However, they ignored the warnings and continued moving towards the Indian side, prompting the BSF personnel to open fire after perceiving a threat.Both were killed in the firing.The intruders' identities are yet to be established. Further proceedings are being carried out in coordination with the Punjab Police and the BSF.The bodies have been handed over to the police for post-mortem examination.A meeting between the BSF and Pakistan Rangers is also expected to be held soon in connection with the incident.
Article Summary: The intruders were trying to cross into Punjab’s Tarn Taran area around noon. BSF troops noticed suspicious movement in the area and challenged the intruders, repeatedly warning them to stop. They ignored the warnings and continued moving towards the Indian side, prompting the BSF personnel to open fire.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. NEW DELHI: Around 1,500 pilgrims stranded on the Kedarnath route near Chirbasa were safely rescued and escorted to Gaurikund after a landslide blocked the route late Sunday night, officials said.The pilgrims were stranded around three kilometres from Gaurikund after a landslide hit the route near Chirbasa, news agency ANI reported.The Rudraprayag District Control Room (DCR) informed Sonprayag Police about the situation late on September 27, following which the SDRF Sonprayag team, led by Sub-Inspector Ashish Dimri, rushed to the spot.Prioritising the safety of the pilgrims, the rescue teams carefully assisted them across the affected stretch. UJJAIN: A large group of people clashed with police in Ujjain at the spot where a portion of the Shahi Masjid was demolished as part of a road-widening project, news agency ANI reported on Monday.Heavy police force remains deployed in the area.The situation reportedly turned tense when some unidentified individuals began pelting stones in the area. Police personnel intervened to bring the situation under control and fired tear-gas shells to disperse the crowd.The confrontation took place as the Ujjain Municipal Corporation started removing the mosque portion falling within the proposed road alignment for the widening project ahead of Simhastha 2028.Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel are also present at the spot.Earlier, Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav intitaed various develoment works in Ujjain with the demolition activity carried out at his ancestral home.272 structures have been marked for demolition as part of a road-widening project in Ujjain ahead of the Simhastha 2028 fair.Speaking on the occasion, Yadav said the demolition of his childhood home carried personal significance, but was necessary for the larger cause."This is the place where I grew up, playing and running around, and now I am stepping forward to dismantle it with my own hands. It certainly has an emotional impact. However, if it is necessary for the administration and essential for the Simhastha, then this sacrifice must be made. Rape case registered, SIT formed
